evidence.text: Kevin attended clinic today. He has an established diagnosis of focal motor epilepsy.

His seizures typically occur in severe explosive clusters rather than isolated events. On 5 and 6 February 2025, over a 48-hour period, he suffered an acute cluster of 5 focal motor seizures with left facial and arm clonic activity. He had no seizures between that cluster and today's review. He reports no convulsions. He continues carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily.
No changes were made to his regimen. No EEG requested. Review in four months.
I reviewed Kevin in clinic today. His diagnosis remains focal motor epilepsy on carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily.
He experienced a further cluster of 4 focal motor seizures over 24 hours on 2 and 3 June 2025. Between clusters he remains entirely seizure-free. The two patterns are discussed separately below.
Management maintained. Follow-up in four months.
Kevin attended for review. He suffered another cluster of 6 focal motor seizures over two days on 15 and 16 September 2025. No events since.
Carbamazepine continued. Routine review in six months.

A second pattern consists of brief bilateral arm shaking without facial involvement. These shaking episodes and his focal motor clusters have both recurred since November 2024, including throughout January and early February. I currently regard both as epileptic. These are the only two patterns reported since November; they are distinct events.

A second pattern consists of brief bilateral arm shaking without facial involvement. These shaking episodes and his focal motor clusters have both recurred since November 2024, including throughout January and early February. I currently regard both as epileptic. These are the only two patterns reported since November; they are distinct events.

The brief bilateral arm shaking is the same second pattern described as epileptic in February; it recurred on 21 May 2025. On review today, 20 June, I explicitly reclassify all of those shaking events, including the February episodes, as functional non-epileptic events. This is the first change from an epileptic to a non-epileptic interpretation in his record, and it was decided today, not earlier. The focal motor clusters remain epileptic and are the only epileptic pattern active since November 2024.
